reuse.why: The rule changes go into the existing getScheduledAmount, but the API's expectedAmount re-implements the expected-amount rule inline in scheduleModel.toExternal instead of calling that shared helper.

duplication.why: The expected-amount rule now exists twice (getScheduledAmount and the nested ternary in api-models.ts), and the copies already disagree: the API copy keeps the step-2 furthest-from-zero rule and ignores approximate amounts.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts where it belongs, but a second version of it sits in the API model mapping layer, which should only translate fields.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the schedule amount rule, the API model, its handler types and tests; the now-unused rangeRounding parameter and stale midpoint concept are left behind rather than cleaned up.

maintainability.why: A maintainer must keep two diverging rule definitions in sync, getScheduledAmount carries a dead rangeRounding parameter, and the approximate rule only applies at the one caller that remembers to pass amountOp as a loose string.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount with its own ternary instead of getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount, ..., schedule._amountOp).

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts expectedAmount: the range-endpoint selection is rewritten as a nested Math.abs ternary rather than shared with getScheduledAmount, and has drifted from it.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount gains an optional `amountOp?: string` parameter and an `isapprox` branch, while the old rangeRounding parameter becomes dead; only computeSchedulePreviewTransactions passes amountOp (the other ~12 callers in forecast, schedules/app, schedule-template and desktop-client do not), and api-models.ts toExternal bypasses the helper entirely.
